analysis:
This batch contains only documentation: a new changelog entry (changelog.d/qwen-end-of-prompt-checkpoints.md, lines 1-13) and docs/architecture/inference.md (date bump at line 3, one new config-table row near head line 1387 for `demandedLatestCheckpointMinimumTokens`). No executable code is in this batch, so no code-level regression can be shown here. The docs describe a behavior change in the provider's SSD prefix-cache path (T-041, TB-007, A-001). For dense Qwen 3.5/3.8, a solo prefill now ends a range just below the prompt end (at least 64 tokens before it, 256-token grid, when it saves at least 1,024 tokens). That adds one more complete SSD checkpoint per request at a deeper token boundary. Security-relevant points for integration:
(1) The checkpoint should go through the same encrypted DBK3 store, HMAC lookup tags, cacheSalt scoping, 30-minute sliding TTL and per-donation adoption/benefit gating described in T-041. It must not add plaintext prompt-derived metadata. That is not verifiable from this documentation-only batch, so the Swift change (EngineV2Factory+DemandedCheckpoint.swift and the engine-loop range planning) needs review against T-041 (a)-(e).
(2) The extra checkpoint near the prompt end slightly widens the same-account TTFT oracle (SEC-035) and may increase disk write volume and endurance consumption. Both are within the existing accepted-risk and endurance guards, assuming the donation gates apply.
(3) The claim of identical outputs relies on the bit-exact recurrent state assumption for Gated DeltaNet checkpoints, which is a correctness concern rather than a confidentiality one.
No new trust boundary, endpoint or secret handling is introduced in the supplied text. I raise no findings. I set needs_deeper_review because the actual code that implements this behavior is outside the supplied evidence.
